Messages.Author: John M. Baker

<snpDpdm00...@andrew.cmu.edu>...

> Excerpts from netnews.rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad: 22-Jul-97 Anarch
> Revolt by Michael Be...@leila.ping.

> > Is Anarch Revolt cumulative?
>
> No. Redundant, but not cumulative. Just like Army of Rats.

Actually, only Army of Rats has the "not cumulative" errata. Anarch
Revolt does not have such errata, and it's generally played that it is
cumulative.

John Baker

Messages.Author: LSJ (VtES Rep)
Messages.Body:
James A Ignatuk wrote:
>
> Excerpts from netnews.rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad: 22-Jul-97 Anarch
> Revolt by Michael Be...@leila.ping.
> > Is Anarch Revolt cumulative?
>
> No. Redundant, but not cumulative. Just like Army of Rats.

Anarch Revolts are cumulative. If ten are in play, then each Methuselah
loses ten pool during her untap.

(Army of Rats are not cumulative, as Mr. Ignatuk says)

--

Messages.Author: James A Ignatuk
Messages.Body:
Excerpts from netnews.rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad: 23-Jul-97 Re:
Anarch Revolt by VtES R...@regency.wizards

> Anarch Revolts are cumulative. If ten are in play, then each Methuselah
> loses ten pool during her untap.
>
> (Army of Rats are not cumulative, as Mr. Ignatuk says)

Sorry, I figured since Anarch Revolt is worded exactly as Army of
Rats is (i.e. it says "lose 1 pool during untap" as opposed to "an
additional pool"), then the ruling would be the same. My apologies for
any confusion...

Take care,
Jim

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In article <33D463...@leila.ping.de>, Michael Beer
<Mi...@leila.ping.de> writes
>Is Anarch Revolt cumulative?
>

Card Title: Anarch Revolt
Pool: n/a
Clan/Discip.: n/a
Card Type: Master
Card Text: Master
Put this card in play. Each Methuselah burns 1 pool
during his or her untap phase. Any vampire can burn
this card with a successful vote; calling this vote is a
+1 stealth action.
Artist: Pete Venters
Rarity: Uncommon

Hmm, it's one of those awkward cards. I'd have to say yes, because
since it would be cumulative with other cards eg Antediluvian Awakening,
I see no reason why not with itself.

--

James Coupe (remove .nospam to reply)
